policy: PMIDs are disjoint from calibration_v1; curated summaries were written before final evaluation and labels are frozen.

records.benchmark_text: Lavender oil was significantly superior to placebo in reducing anxiety symptoms in adults with subsyndromal anxiety.
Ginger was effective for relief of mild to moderate nausea and vomiting in early pregnancy.
Cranberry capsules showed no significant difference from placebo in bacteriuria plus pyuria or symptomatic urinary tract infections.
Cranberry juice did not significantly reduce urinary tract infection risk compared with placebo.
Cranberry products did not significantly reduce symptomatic urinary tract infections overall and could not be recommended for prevention.
Clinical-trial evidence suggests cranberry does not seem to be effective in preventing or treating urinary tract infections in spinal cord injury.
Silymarin improved several clinical symptoms and indirect bilirubin, but liver enzymes and other biomarkers were not significantly reduced.
Ginger significantly improved general pregnancy nausea and vomiting symptoms and nausea versus placebo, but had no significant effect on vomiting.
